newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee scoops new losses on funds sell-off.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee scoops new losses on funds sell-off.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures scooped new losses in late dealings after persistent fund and trade long liquidation triggered fresh sell-stops at $1,340 basis January. Traders said there was also nervous selling by the origins. The speculative community also liquidated some of their long positions amid diminishing prospects of a rebound in prices and coupled with easing tightness in nearby supplies.
"Overall, the coffee picture is not that bullish," said one.

While there was no immediate news or rumours driving the market lower, traders said the background fundamental outlook for robusta coffee remained poor on the back of a seasonal rise in African and Asian production.
Traders said the avalanche of selling orders were also sparked by the weakness in November on the expiry at lunch today as initial fears of a small supply squeeze on the spot month evaporated.
Benchmark January lost $16 to end Friday at $1,336 a tonne after a low of $1,331, the lowest level since March 1994.
In all, the second-month position had lost a hefty 4.2 percent since Thursday morning.
Traders were divided on the immediate market prospects, with some saying that the selling could have been overdone while others said there was still some room on the downside.
Some noted that players would be wary of going short into the weekend especially if New York fails to open sharply lower on resumption on Monday.

The U.S. market is closed for a long Thanksgiving holiday. Overall volume reached 5,853 lots, concentrated mainly on January and March contracts as some operators rolled forward their nearby positions.
